## Writing with MDX

The entire document is composed from MDX sections. Ordinary Markdown goes through a shared component map; interactive examples use the same components as the rest of the documentation.

### Text and hierarchy

Paragraphs use Inter at 16 px with a 1.625 line height. **Emphasis is quiet**, _italics remain available_, and ~~deleted text~~ keeps its usual meaning. Inline `code` uses Ioskeley Mono Medium.

#### A third-level heading

Headings preserve their semantic levels. The 672 px column sits inside a 768 px frame on larger screens. Text uses 16 px insets; cards, tables, and code fill their rows.

##### A fourth-level heading

Keep subsections short and use descriptive links, like [the controller reference](#api-reference).

###### A fifth-level heading

Additional heading levels remain available for deeply structured references.

###### A sixth-level heading

Every heading can be linked directly.

### Lists and quotes

- Use a normal list for related ideas.
- Nest a list when the relationship needs it.
  - Keep the child close to its parent.

1. Register a target.
2. Define a rule.
3. Handle its prediction.

- [x] Semantic Markdown components
- [x] Code highlighted at build time
- [ ] A real task that has not been completed

> A prediction is only useful if the interface still works when it is wrong.

### Code and tables

Fenced code is highlighted by Shiki and includes a copy control. Long lines scroll inside the block.

```ts
const condition = { type: 'intersects', withinMs: 120 } as const;
```

| Element   | Rendering                                    |
| :-------- | :------------------------------------------- |
| Paragraph | Comfortable measure and consistent spacing   |
| Code      | Shiki, light and dark themes, copy button    |
| Table     | Bordered container with horizontal scrolling |
| Image     | Rounded corners and a subtle outline         |

### Useful HTML

Use <kbd className="rounded border border-b-2 bg-card px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-xs text-foreground">Tab</kbd> to move between controls. You can use <mark className="rounded bg-emerald-100 px-1 text-emerald-950 dark:bg-emerald-950 dark:text-emerald-100">highlighted text</mark>, <abbr className="underline decoration-dotted underline-offset-4" title="Estimated time of arrival">ETA</abbr>, x<sup className="text-xs">2</sup>, and x<sub className="text-xs">0</sub> when they clarify a reference.

<dl className="my-6">
  <dt className="mt-5 font-medium text-foreground">Horizon</dt>
  <dd className="mt-1 mb-5 ml-5">How far into the future the controller projects movement.</dd>
  <dt className="mt-5 font-medium text-foreground">Margin</dt>
  <dd className="mt-1 mb-5 ml-5">The extra area around a target rectangle.</dd>
</dl>

<Details>
  <Summary>Which Markdown elements are mapped?</Summary>

All CommonMark and GFM output elements: headings, paragraphs, links, images, lists, blockquotes, code, thematic breaks, emphasis, deletion, tables, task inputs, and footnotes. The map also covers figures, captions, definition lists, disclosure elements, keyboard text, abbreviations, subscript, superscript, audio, and video.

</Details>

<Callout title="Shared components">

The MDX provider owns typography, code blocks, links, media, and tables. Changing a shared component updates every section without editing its prose.

</Callout>

### Footnotes

Footnotes work with the GFM pipeline and keep their return links.[^geometry]

[^geometry]: The documentation describes geometric prediction; it does not claim to predict a user’s intent.
